Bill.BriefDescription: Reducing the size of the state supreme court.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to the size of the state supreme court; andamending RCW 2.04.070 and 2.04.071.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 2.04.070 and 1909 c 24 s 1 are each amended to read asfollows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: When a vacancy on the supreme court occurs by death, resignation,or otherwise after the effective date of this section, it may not befilled until the number of judges on that court has been reduced toseven. Thereafter, the supreme court((, from and after February 26,1909,)) shall consist of ((nine)) seven judges. A vacancy can occur by resignation, retirement, death, orotherwise.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 2.04.071 and 1971 c 81 s 1 are each amended to read asfollows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: ((At the next general election, and at each biennial generalelection thereafter, there shall be elected three justices of thesupreme court, to hold for the full term of six years, and until theirsuccessors are elected and qualified)) Upon the reduction in size of p. 1 SB 6088the supreme court from nine to seven justices, no fewer than two and nomore than three judges may be elected at each biennial general electionto serve sixyear terms, commencing with the second Monday in Januarysucceeding their election.
